summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 14.4% to INR 434.12 crore and PAT 35.61% to INR 43.84 crore; management reiterates 30-35% CAGR target.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 total revenue of INR 434.12 crore (+14.4% YoY), EBITDA of INR 61.35 crore (+23.34%) and PAT of INR 43.84 crore (+35.61%), against an internal target of INR 430 crore revenue and INR 40 crore PAT. The Bhilwara 10,000 MT R-32 plant received environmental clearance and is guided to start production by October 2026. Q4 revenue of about INR 110 crore was flat-to-down versus prior quarters, which analysts questioned; management attributed this to LPG and energy disruptions hitting end-customer industries. Management reiterated 30-35% revenue CAGR and 3-4% margin improvement over three years, with FY27 PAT guided at about INR 100 crore and a 2030 aspiration of INR 3,000 crore revenue and INR 500 crore PAT.

segments.name: Fluorochemicals / refrigerants (R-32, HFO blends)
segments.commentary: Management said R-32 prices are INR 800-900/kg currently versus its INR 500-550/kg planning assumption; the company has largely exited domestic R-32 sales (from over 4,500 MT two years ago to 400-500 MT now) due to low margins.

segments.name: Specialty and high-purity gases (helium, semiconductor gases)
segments.commentary: Khalapur helium plant is in final testing with start-up expected next month (around June 2026); helium prices reportedly moved from INR 800-900 to above INR 3,000-4,000 per unit as cited by management, with supply tightness from Qatar.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR target of 30-35% over next three years with margin improvement of 3-4%.

FY27 revenue: management cited about INR 275 crore from R-32 over six months of operation plus the existing business, implying about INR 430 crore base; FY27 PAT estimated at about INR 100 crore (40 crore base plus about 60 crore from new capacity at 22% PAT).
H1 FY27 PAT margins expected to be similar to last year's levels; H2 margins expected to rise about 5-6 percentage points as manufacturing (22-24% PAT margin) contributes about 50% of growth.
Long-term aspiration by 2030: INR 3,000 crore revenue and INR 500 crore PAT; with R-32 fully operational, revenue should cross INR 1,100-1,200 crore with about INR 180 crore PAT.
HFO manufacturing plant (capex cited as INR 200 crore in MoU, stated as pure plant and machinery; total capex about INR 400 crore) to start only after Bhilwara stabilises, post mid-FY27.
capex_capacity: Bhilwara, Rajasthan: 10,000 MT R-32 plant; environmental clearance received; production expected by October 2026; capital work in progress about INR 35 crore, with management saying payments will rise as equipment is delivered (20-30% advances, 70% on delivery, 30% on commissioning).
Khalapur, Maharashtra: helium and liquid helium/semiconductor gas facility in final testing; start-up expected around June 2026.

Mumbattu, Andhra Pradesh: South India facility for HFO/HFC blending, de-bulking, helium and semiconductor gas handling; scaled from an IPO plan of 5 bulk tanks to 12 tanks; operational by August 2026 per management.
HFO manufacturing plant: management said to start after Bhilwara is stabilised (post mid-FY27); no further dilution envisaged after the rights issue.
Company operates four facilities with two more under development, supported by a pan-India distribution network.
demand_pricing: R-32 prices currently INR 800-900/kg (bulk), roughly double earlier levels; other products up about 15-20% per management.
Management expects Indian refrigerant/air-conditioning demand to grow 10-15% YoY for the next 10 years; Indian market for R-32 cited at 20,000-22,000 MT.
Industry capacity: management cited about 40,000-50,000 MT of additional R-32 capacity coming up in India, designed largely for exports; China HFC capacity cited at about 800,000 MT.
Q4 top-line flat-to-lower attributed to LPG shortages and supply-chain disruption hitting end-customer industries rather than pricing.
Quota: management expects 10,000 MT quota allocation for the Bhilwara plant; government policy expected in FY27, details not yet released.
No pre-contracts or offtake agreements signed for R-32; management said it sees no need for tie-ups at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the rights entitlement sold rather than applied for, and why has shareholding fallen?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said shares sold were bought back, and the dilution (about 68%) reflected an issue price of INR 99 rather than the INR 140 initially planned; current holding stated at about 47.5% or a little more.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30-35% growth target on track given FY26 growth of 14% and a sharp QoQ revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target was INR 430 crore revenue and INR 40 crore PAT for FY26, which was surpassed; 30-35% growth is for the next three years; FY27 needs about INR 560 crore for 30% growth and is expected to exceed it if R-32 starts on time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing and revenue contribution from Khalapur and Mumbattu, and the HFO plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Khalapur start-up expected around June; Mumbattu by August; no separate revenue figure given for these sites. HFO plant to start after Bhilwara is stabilised, post mid-FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Bhilwara CWIP only about INR 35 crore against a roughly INR 200 crore capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Company pays 20-30% advances only, with balance on delivery and commissioning; orders placed for almost all equipment, so payments should rise significantly this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Saudi helium tie-up and Qatar disruption affect sourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Sharjah Oxygen tie-up is strategic; Qatar helium output is curtailed, but helium prices have risen sharply, which management views as an opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 PAT margins and the assumed R-32 price?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 FY27 margins similar to prior year; H2 up about 5-6 points; FY27 PAT about INR 100 crore based on INR 500-550/kg R-32 pricing, below the current INR 900/kg.

risks_watch: Commissioning delays at Bhilwara (October 2026), Khalapur and Mumbattu; analysts noted a possible one-to-two month slip, which management said higher prices could offset.
Government R-32 quota allocation (10,000 MT assumed) not yet released; policy expected in FY27.
Q4 revenue of about INR 110 crore versus INR 150 crore in the prior-year quarter; management attributes this to LPG and energy disruption affecting customers.
Margin pressure in H1 FY27 from higher oil and LPG costs; management said margins 'would be highly strained'.
Large cash balance (about INR 434 crore) is largely earmarked for capex; working capital not funded by the rights issue; cash deployment and unused credit limit to be monitored.
Shareholding dilution and rights issue execution; analyst questioned consistency of rights application commitments.
Management's use of unaudited growth targets and differing capex figures (INR 200 crore vs INR 400 crore total); guidance clarity to be monitored.
summary.management_tone: Confident and combative, particularly in rebutting analyst questions on growth, shareholding and rights issue; management repeatedly stressed foresight and conservatism but gave few hard numbers on Mumbattu/Khalapur revenue and quota allocation, and deflected on tie-ups and government policy.
key_quotes: Onwards going 30-35% growth is there for the next three years which we have always been saying and I still continue saying
The H1 margins would be conversant with the last year's same percentages.
Our target figures are by 2030 we want to have INR 3,000 crore revenue and we want to have a PAT of INR 500 crore.
We regret not putting double the capacity.
